sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Rahul Sahai Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in case crime No. 707 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201, 120-B, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Highway,
District Mathura, with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
The applicant is husband of deceased.

The first information report has been lodged after two days of the incident and that after the incident, the parental family of deceased has reached at the spot but at that time, no report was lodged.

It was submitted that before the incident,
the deceased was working in Australia and that the total income of deceased and applicant was around 26 lakhs per month and thus, the allegation regarding dowry demand, is thoroughly false and improbable.

It was submitted that in fact deceased wanted to marry with someone else and she Rahul vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145527969/
1 has committed suicide due to that reason.

entities.text: she Rahul vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, during trial statement of informant has already been recorded, wherein he has not supported the prosecution version and turned hostile.

Lastly, it is submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 16.09.2022, and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate in the trial.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and argued that deceased has suffered unnatural death within a short period of about 4-5 months of her marriage and some material witnesses are yet to be examined before the trial Court.
There are allegations that the deceased was being harassed on account of dowry.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, gravity of offence and all attending facts and circumstances of case, the applicant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the bail application of applicant Rahul is hereby rejected.
